evals.prompt: I'm building an invoice payment agent in Python. It needs to: (1) load a wallet from an env var called XRPL_WALLET_SEED, (2) check the XRP balance on testnet, (3) send 50 XRP to rPT1Sjq2YGrBMTttX4GZHjKu9dyfzbpAYe, and (4) print the transaction hash. Show me complete, runnable code.
evals.expected_output: Complete Python script using xrpl-py that loads wallet from env var, checks balance with drops_to_xrp, sends 50 XRP using xrp_to_drops and submit_and_wait, and prints tesSUCCESS result and hash.
expectations: Uses xrp_to_drops(50) for the payment amount — not a raw float or integer
Uses submit_and_wait (not submit) for the payment transaction
Loads wallet from os.environ['XRPL_WALLET_SEED'] or os.environ.get()
Connects to the testnet RPC endpoint (s.altnet.rippletest.net)
Prints or returns the transaction hash from response.result['hash']
Uses drops_to_xrp when displaying the balance

evals.prompt: My AI agent needs to pay vendors in RLUSD on XRPL testnet. The wallet seed is in XRPL_WALLET_SEED. Walk me through (1) setting up the RLUSD trust line and (2) sending 250 RLUSD to rN7n3473SaZBCG4dFL83w7PB5AMtQFfDgE. Give me Python code for both steps.
evals.expected_output: Python code with TrustSet using RLUSD hex currency code and issuer, then Payment using IssuedCurrencyAmount. Both use submit_and_wait. Trust line noted as one-time setup.
expectations: Includes a TrustSet transaction to establish the RLUSD trust line
Uses IssuedCurrencyAmount for the RLUSD payment amount
References the RLUSD hex currency code (524C555344000000000000000000000000000000) or notes it must be confirmed
Uses submit_and_wait for both the TrustSet and Payment transactions
Makes clear the trust line is a one-time setup step
Does not pass raw string 'RLUSD' as currency without noting the hex encoding requirement

evals.prompt: I'm building a compliance-aware payment agent on XRPL. Every payment my agent makes needs to be traceable — I want to tag all agent transactions with a source tag, and embed the agent ID, session ID, and invoice ID in the transaction so I can correlate on-chain activity with my app logs. Show me Python code that sends 30 XRP with this audit metadata attached.
evals.expected_output: Python code with source_tag integer on Payment, hex-encoded JSON Memo containing agent_id/session_id/invoice_id, using submit_and_wait and xrp_to_drops from xrpl.utils.
expectations: Sets source_tag to an integer on the Payment transaction
Includes a Memos field with a Memo object containing memo_data
Hex-encodes the memo data (using base64.b16encode or similar)
The memo content includes multiple fields (agent ID, session ID, and at least one task/invoice identifier)
Uses xrp_to_drops for the XRP amount
